Forme juridique de l'attributaire Le marché public sera conclu : – soit avec un opérateur économique unique ; 8/17 – soit avec un groupement d’opérateurs économiques conjoint ou solidaire. En cas de groupement conjoint, le mandataire sera solidaire, pour l'exécution du marché public, de chacun des membres du groupement, pour ses obligations contractuelles à l'égard de l’acheteur. La composition du groupement ne peut être modifiée entre la remise des offres et la date de signature du contrat. 2-6. ant indiquant qu'il ne tombe pas sous le coup d'une interdiction de soumissionner. Pour satisfaire aux obligations susmentionnées, le candidat qui envisage, dès le dépôt de son offre, de sous-traiter une partie de sa prestation, complètera utilement la déclaration de sous - traitance et joindra, pour chaque sous-traitant, l’ensemble des documents, attestations et renseignements réclamés aux candidats, tels que figurant au présent règlement de la consultation. La notification du marché public emporte acceptation du sous-traitant et agrément des conditions de paiement. Les prestations de services sont prouvées par des attestations du destinataire ou, à défaut, par une déclaration de l'opérateur économique ; • Une déclaration indiquant les effectifs moyens annuels du candidat et l'importance du personnel d'encadrement pendant les trois dernières années ; • Une description de l'outillage, du matériel et de l'équipement technique dont le candidat disposera pour la réalisation du marché public. DSGVO EU verwiesen. 21. Ergänzende Hinweise zum Thema Datenschutz Die einschlägigen datenschutzrechtlichen Bestimmungen werden eingehalten. Es wird daher erwartet, dass das Verfahren bei der Verarbeitung der Daten die Vorgaben der DS-GVO einhält und dies durch eine entsprechende anerkannte Zertifizierung von Produkt und Prozess nachweist. Es wird erwartet, dass sämtliche Maßnahmen zur Unterstützung der Datenschutzfolgeabschätzung durch den Beauftragten durchgeführt werden. Insbesondere sind die im Verfahrensverzeichnis aufzunehmenden verfahrensbe- zogenen Angaben zur Verfügung zu stellen (vgl. Art. 30 DS-GVO). Daher werden die aktuellen techni- schen und organisatorischen Maßnahmen des Anbieters angefordert. Im Verfahren werden regelmäßig personenbezogene Daten verarbeitet. Die Zulässigkeit der Verarbeitung personenbezogener Daten richtet sich nach den einschlägigen datenschutzrechtlichen Vorschriften. Vor der Entscheidung über den Einsatz e

en datenschutzrechtlichen Vorschriften. Vor der Entscheidung über den Einsatz eines automatisierten Verfahrens sind ggf. im Rahmen einer Daten- schutzfolgeabschätzung (Art. 35 DS-GVO), die die zur Bewältigung der Risiken geplanten Abhilfemaß- nahmen, einschließlich Garantien, Sicherheitsvorkehrungen und Verfahren, durch die der Schutz perso- nenbezogener Daten sichergestellt durch den Verantwortlichen zu dokumentieren. Dies bildet den Nach- weis über die Einhaltung der DSGVO. Die IT- und TK-Verantwortung obliegt innerhalb der Stadt Essen der eigenbetriebsähnlichen Einrichtung „Essener Systemhaus“. Das Essener Systemhaus ist zertifiziert nach ISO 27001. Si le candidat adresse plusieurs offres différentes, seule la dernière offre reçue, dans les conditions du présent règlement, sera examinée. Article premier : Objet et étendue de la consultation 1.1 - Objet de la consultation Le CROUS de Montpellier assure des services d’hébergement et de restauration pour les étudiants de l’académie de Montpellier. references_experience.text: (MVVM) development pattern, where you would have to code the presentation layer by creating View Models and Views for each object you wish to display, using NOF there is only a set of default generic (MVVM) views defined by NOF and they are applied to all domain objects (models). The Naked Objects pattern was first described formally in Richard Pawson's PhD thesis which includes a thorough investigation of various antecedents and inspirations for the pattern including, for example, the Morphic user interface. Naked Objects is commonly contrasted with the model-view-controller pattern. However, the published version of Pawson's thesis (see References) contains a foreword by Trygve Reenskaug, who first formulated the model-view-controller pattern, suggesting that Naked Objects is closer to the original intent of model-view-controller than many of the subsequent interpretations and implementations. Further information on the NO pattern is available at http://www.nakedobjects.org/ . Naked Objects 2.0 The BOMi currently uses version 2.0 of the Naked Objects framework, referred to as 'NOF2', which was the first publicly available framework to implement the 'naked objects pattern'. NOF2 was originally written by Naked Objects Group and supplied to the Department under an open-source licence.

Our strategy sets a clear pathway to achieve net zero emissions in a way that supports our customers and ensures ESB’s continued growth. ESB are committed to leading the transition to a reliable and affordable net zero future. ESB seeks to purchase supplies, services and works that are produced or delivered in a manner that has the most positive environmental, social and economic impacts possible over their entire lifecycle. ESB procurement processes will be aligned with the standards from ISO20400, Sustainable Procurement. ESB have created a Sustainability Leadership Plan which sets out our ambitions and the actions we will take as they relate to the three pillars of sustainability - People, Planet and Place. Full details of ESB’s Sustainability Leadership Plan can be viewed here: ESB Sustainable Leadership Plan. ESB requires that the successful Contractor emerging from the Procurement process be familiar with our Sustainable Leadership Plan. ESB is a founding member of the Irish Supply Chain Sustainability School. The school’s aim is to support and develop skills and knowledge in sustainability in the built environment. Further

deliverables_scope.text: ie/who-we-are/about-esb A.1.1 General Description of the Proposed Contract The Contracting Entity intends to procure a Digital Learning Design, Development and Maintenance Services framework for the provision of specialist digital learning services, including instructional design, eLearning development, accessibility reviews, project management and associated support services. The successful tenderer will be required to work collaboratively with Subject Matter Experts (SMEs) and stakeholders to design, develop, review, test and deliver digital learning content from initial onboarding through to final approval and provision of SCORM-compliant outputs. The supplier will be expected to provide a structured and transparent development methodology, supported by appropriate governance, project management, universal design principles including accessibility, quality assurance and stakeholder engagement processes. It is proposed that the Framework will include (non-exhaustive list – high level scope): Create engaging, accessible and effective digital learning that keeps learner needs, content and learning objectives central to the design. ip_data_security.text: The Contracting Entity intends to procure a contract for a Service Provider to provide, licence, support and maintenance for ESB’s Digital workspace Monitoring Software. ESB operates the ControlUp monitoring software which enables us to leverage modern digital technologies to gather and analyse data at every critical point of our Digital Workspace infrastructure. It also provides historical data that is very important for recognising trends and proactively addressing issues. It is proposed that the Contract will include (non-exhaustive list – high level scope): ControlUp Performance Monitoring Software The supply of software support with licensing for the existing ESB Digital Workspace solution. Maintenance for all existing software. Management of software licences/subscriptions for all devices and software modules is required. The supply of software support with licensing for any new software added during the term of the contract. This will not be restricted to ControlUp related products as other digital monitoring solutions will be considered. deliverables_scope.text: ESS MODELS Instantly processing data, manufacturers can optimise manufacturing processes and respond faster to changing customer needs – and this ability reconfigures the entire ecosystem. PRODUCT PERSONALISATION AND SERVITISATION The ability to create more product variants while using the same resources is crucial to building a competitive advantage. That’s why increasing production flexibility has long been a pressing matter for manufacturers. Again, data is the game-changer here. Processing real-time information at all stages of user interactions enables creating product simulations that can be adapted to match unique, individual requirements of the customer. Similarly, many manufacturing businesses now expand the value for their clients by shifting from selling products to selling Product-Service Systems (PSS). Pioneered in the 1960s by Rolls Royce, servitisation relieves customers of capital costs, instead offering them advanced solutions in a subscription model. 16 PLATFORMISATION OF PRODUCTION Just as products are now increasingly offered as a service, the manufacturing process is also subject to similar changes. Digital technologies enable breaking it into specific services that can be bought on-demand by other companies (Manufacturing-as-a-Service). Benefitting from

logistics is giving place to digitised distribution enabled by specialised fulfilment centres – very much like in e-commerce. Of course, boosting processes with technology isn’t new. However, what differentiates Logistics 4.0 are progressive datification and smart automation – both translating into increased agility and faster delivery. REORGANISATION OF COMPANIES Industry 4.0 reconfigures the nature of work both in terms of managing both the process and people. The fourth industrial revolution departs from Lean Manufacturing and favours Agile methodologies. Agile Manufacturing focuses on delivering products that closely match clients’ requirements while controlling costs and quality to ensure a relatively low final price and the fastest possible Time to Market. Intelligent technologies help to achieve this objective, so the need for a highly-skilled workforce is also of paramount importance. 3 Michael Mandel, The Rise of the Internet of Goods, available from: http://www.progressivepolicy.org/wp-content/ uploads/2018/08/Internetofgoods-reportPPI-2018.pdf THE RIGHT COMBINATION OF TECHNOLOGIES AND SKILLED WORKFORCE OPENS A MULTITUDE OF BENEFITS TO MANUFACTURERS Increased efficiency and productivity Intelligent technologies allow producing more at lower costs and with less waste.

towards maintaining safe distancing. Improving productivity Manual data collection is prone to errors, especially in times of social distancing and lockdown. Digital solutions allow manufacturers to automate the data collection process by adding sensors or using machines’ programmable logic controllers (PLCs) to collect data and display it on live dashboards. As a result, factories can monitor and act upon performance information remotely and in real- time. At the same time, physical automation and robotics can supplement labour capacity. RESEARCH METHODOLOGY The report features conclusions based on 12 structured, in-depth interviews with representatives of the Industry 4.0 sector in Wroclaw. The main goal was to learn more about how they perceive their current situation – on an individual and collective level. 9 Conducted by an external researcher in September 2020, all interviews were kept anonymous to ensure maximum confidentiality, trust, and openness of the participants. CEOs, managing directors, and senior managers who took part in the survey represent the three different types of organisations: • local production sites and Shared Services Centres (SSC) of international manufacturers; • small, medium and large companies implementing IT solutions – working on software, embedded software, and hardware projects; • a foundation promoting the development of Industry 4.0 in Poland. ON INDUSTRY 4.0 WORLDWIDE Before the outbreak of COVID-19, there was widespread interest in Industry 4.0. The sector’s value was projected to grow up to $3.7 trillion by 20259. However, despite these positive outlooks, the actual landscape of Industry 4.0 adoption has been far more complex. ASPIRATIONS VS REALITY 90% of respondents in McKinsey’s10 annual survey admitted seeing the benefits of digital transformation in manufacturing. A majority of them included introducing new technologies as an essential part of their organisational development strategies. However, as research from the World Economic Forum11 demonstrates, despite these declarations, the reality was still far from this ideal. In 2018, the adoption of technology in production still remained slow across industries and regions. ip_data_security.text: This change wouldn’t be possible without advancements such as the Internet of Things (IoT), the Cloud, Robotic Process Automation (RPA), or Artificial Intelligence (AI). 13 Therefore, this publication follows the BCG’s definition of Industry 4.01, seeing it as a transformation that enables analysing data across machines and using it for more efficient manufacturing at reduced costs. CORE TECHNOLOGIES SUPPORTING INDUSTRY 4.0 Autonomous robots & cobots Digital Twins & simulation The AI-powered cloud Augmented & virtual reality Digital integration systems The Industrial Internet of Things Additive manufacturing Big Data & analytics Cybersecurity * ORGANISED AFTER THE BOSTON CONSUL TING GROUP Apart from increasing productivity, Industry 4.0 also encourages developing new products and business models. As a result, it modifies the workforce profile and reconfigures the competitiveness of companies and regions. These issues will be discussed later on in this chapter but first, let’s focus on the three core advancements differentiating Industry 4.0 from the previous revolutions. DATIFICATION Integrating data from devices, sensors, and IT systems enables developing new solutions at all stages of the product lifecycle – from design to production, logistics and maintenance. 1

ntinuously collecting, analysing, and using data in real-time. IIoT enables monitoring of all production processes and scheduling maintenance accordingly. When integrating Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES), Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP), and Customer Relationship Management (CRM), the network allows for comprehensive management of all related operations. THE CONVERGENCE OF IT SYSTEMS AND OPERATIONAL TECHNOLOGY (OT) In the past, IT and OT worked as separate entities: the first one mostly serving management, the latter controlling machines and resources. Thanks to the IIoT, these two worlds have been increasingly converging. Cyber-physical systems (CPS) embody this tendency as machines now combine both the IT and operational qualities. One of the most advanced CP systems – Digital Twins – enables creating digital replicas of physical objects but also processes based on data collected from sensors. ROBOTISATION AND AUTOMATION Industry 4.0 is also underpinned by a growing level of robotisation and automation. Apart from automated production lines, factories now boast autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) and collaborative robots (cobots). Kui hankemenetlusest kõrvaldamise alus esineb, võib ettevõtja soovi korral esitada tõendeid selle kohta, et ta on võtnud meetmeid oma usaldusväärsuse taastamiseks. Heastamise võim

Website Hosting & Support Service The objective of this tender process is to invite proposals for the provision of website hosting, ongoing maintenance and development services for the CORU website. Tenderers shall demonstrate their capability to provide a secure, reliable, and resilient hosting environment that supports the continued availability and performance of the website. Particular consideration will be given to: • The location of the hosting infrastructure and the suitability of the hosting arrangement from a regulatory, operational, and data governance perspective. • The provision of secure and user -friendly content management functionality that enables authorised CORU staff to undertake routine and moderate website content updates without requiring specialist technical support. • The implementation of appropriate security controls, monitoring, and maintenance processes to protect the website from unauthorised access, modification, disruption, or malicious activi

Website Migration Services The successful tenderer shall be responsible for the migration of CORU's existing live website to the proposed hosting environment. The migration service shall include, at a minimum: • Development and execution of a detailed migration plan, including timelines, responsibilities, testing and implementation activities. • Migration of all website content, functionality, configurations and associated assets to the proposed environment. • Measures to minimise disruption to website availability and user experience during the migration process. • Comprehensive testing prior to go -live, including functional, security, performance, accessibility and user acceptance testing. • Provision of rollback and recovery procedures in the event of migration issues. • Preservation of existing search engine rankings and implementation of any necessary redirects and SEO protections during migration. • Post-migration support to address any issues arising following implementation. The Contractor shall deliver fully operational, integrated, and sustained EW SITE systems and sub-system components for domestic and Foreign Military Sales (FMS) customers. The intent is to ensure the Contractor performs In Accordance With (IAW) the Performance Work Statement (PWS) and the Government receives the quality of services called for in the FFP contract. The Contractor shall deliver fully operational, integrated, and sustained EW SITE systems and sub-system components for domestic and Foreign Military Sales (FMS) customers. The required outcome is an EW SITE system capable of supporting a multitude of laboratory-specific System Configurations across multiple platforms (EA-18G, F/A-18, MH-60) while maintaining configuration consistency with the Advanced Weapons Laboratory (AWL) at NAWCWD China Lake, CA. Additionally, the Contractor shall ensure continuous operational readiness of current EW SITE systems through comprehensive lifecycle support, including on-call and on-site maintenance, system upgrades, replacement parts provisioning, and personnel training. This Contract will have FFP CLINs. The Contract will have a five-year period of performance. A properly executed QASP will assist the Government in achieving the objectives of this procurement. 2. insurance_bonds.text: EMENT OF OBJECTIVES (SOO) For Secure by-Design Space Vehicle (SDSV) Topic Area 3 1.0 Purpose The objective of this effort is to address cyber threats to national critical space missions (e.g., Position, Navigation, and Timing (PNT), Missile Warning/Missile Tracking (MW/MT), Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance (ISR), and Satellite Communications (SATCOM)) through the research, design, development, testing, and demonstration of a comprehensive Secure by-Design Space Vehicle (SDSV) system. 2.0 Background Space vehicles are increasingly recognized as vulnerable platforms facing sophisticated cyber threats. To ensure mission assurance, there is a critical need to provide advanced defensive solutions for space assets. This project aims to reduce the attack surfaces of space vehicles and implement robust resiliency mechanisms that enable self-protection and rapid recovery from cyber anomalies, leveraging Cyber-Hardened Satellite Software (CHSS) technology. 3.0 Period and Place of Performance • Period of Performance: The anticipated period of performance is a 12-month Base effort, followed by three (3) 12-month Option periods, plus 3 months for final reporting (Total 51 Months). • Place of Performance: The work will be performed primarily at the contractors facilit

The space vehicle build will be conducted at TBD contractor location, the cyber-hardening will be conducted at MITLL and T&E conducted at AFRL KAFB SCR. 4.0 Performance Objectives The Government's objective is to achieve the following capabilities and milestones across the period of performance. The contractor shall propose the specific methodology and detailed work breakdown to achieve these objectives: Phase Technical Objectives & Deliverables Base Period (Months 1- 12): System Design, Development, and Initial Hardening Design & Build: Design and construct a space vehicle flat-sat and a corresponding space vehicle cyber range. The following factors shall be used to evaluate offers: Lowest Price Technically Acceptable - Offers will be ranked lowest to highest according to price. A price analysis will be conducted to determine whether the lowest price will result from a single award or multiple awards. Based on the price analysis, the lowest price offer or multiple offers, will be forwarded to the requiring activity for technical evaluation (offer(s), in accordance with the specifications, will be deemed either technically acceptable or technically unacceptable). If the lowest price offer or offers is found technically acceptable and the pricing determined fair and reasonable by the Contracting Officer, evaluation will be deemed complete and award will be made based on the lowest price offer(s). If the lowest price offer is determined technically unacceptable, another analysis will be conducted amongst the remaining offers to determine if a single or multiple awards will provide the lowest price. Warranty coverage shall include the processor, motherboard, memory, storage devices, power supply, cooling components, chassis, and all four installed GPUs. The contractor shall identify warranty duration, support procedures, and replacement or repair timelines in its proposal. Contractor Responsibilities The contractor is responsible for verifying final component compatibility before shipment, including but not limited to: - CPU-to-motherboard compatibility; - PCIe lane availability and GPU slot configuration; - GPU physical dimensions and slot spacing; - Power draw and connector requirements; - Thermal performance under multi-GPU loads; - Chassis airflow and component clearance; and - Driver and operating-system compatibility. entity_geography.text: plemental plan may offer some augmentation but should aim to avoid full duplication of what is currently available through the national healthcare system. When preparing a competitive quotation, vendors should take into consideration benefits provided through the national healthcare system. Quotations should refrain from over customization, and should be “off the shelf”, “commercially available”, or “market ready” products which are designed to be complementary and supplement to the national system in Portugal. The benefit levels listed from section C.1.1 through C.1.24 are a standard package that must be provided. C.1.1 Eligibility: To be eligible to participate in the medical plan, LE Staff (both full time and part time) must be: -- Paid under the terms of the Local Compensation Plan (LCP); and – -- Under a non-temporary direct hire appointment, personal services agreement (PSA), or personal services contract (PSC); or -- Under a temporary direct hire appointment or PSA Fixed Term of one year or more. Not eligible are those working under temporary appointments; those working under a PSC or PSA that is time limited to less than one year; non-personal services contract personnel and their employees, supplied by an independent contractor l

ents; those working under a PSC or PSA that is time limited to less than one year; non-personal services contract personnel and their employees, supplied by an independent contractor licensed to do business in Portugal who provides services to other local RFP 19GE5026Q0035-0001 – LES Health Insurance Services for U.S. Embassy Lisbon Page 6 of 21 organizations as well as to the U.S. Mission; employees working on an intermittent or When Actually Employed (WAE) schedule; Peace Corps personal services contractors and Recreation Association employees. C.1.2 Riders: There are no riders under this contract. C.1.3 Periods of Ineligibility: Employees and their dependents are not entitled to health benefits during any period of employment for which premiums are not paid. Additionally, employee's dependents are not entitled to health benefits during any period of employment during which the employee was not eligible to participate. During a period of extended Leave Without Pay (LWOP) or other unpaid leave beyond one pay period, the employee is responsible for the full cost of the insurance premiums for self and dependents. Commissioning: Commissioning is a process that involves the entire Design Team throughout the planning, design, construction and occupancy of the project. Commissioning Guidelines for AOC Projects are contained in the policy statement of June 7, 2010. During the initial planning process, the AOC Project Team shall determine the purpose and role of commissioning.
